summary: Intermittent iam:PassRole AccessDenied for deployment-runner during staged GPU provisioning
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-08 we have observed intermittent AccessDenied errors (iam:PassRole) from the deployment-runner when creating GPU instances in staging that require cross-account role pass-through. Impact: Provisioning jobs for Dedicated staging pools fail ~10-15% of attempts causing test rollouts to stall and PR gates to back up. This is blocking multiple engineering teams who validate autoscaling and rollback behavior against the staging cluster.

Environment: staging account (aws: 123456789012), us-west-2, deployment-runner service (k8s job) invoking Provisioner Lambda which calls STS AssumeRole -> EC2 RunInstances with iam:PassRole.

High-level timeline: failures first reported by on-call infra test runs on 2026-03-08 02:00 UTC and continue intermittently through 2026-03-13.

Requested outcome: determine root cause, implement a reliable fix or robust retry/backoff, and produce a short runbook for on-call and release engineers.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a staging dedicated-provision pipeline that launches GPU-backed nodes via deployment-runner (use staging-gpu pipeline).
Observe the Provisioner Lambda logs and the deployment-runner controller logs for failures during the EC2 RunInstances call.
Run the repro in a tight loop (10-20 iterations) to surface intermittent failures; failure rate observed ~10-15%.
When failure occurs, capture the Provisioner Lambda trace_id and STS token timestamps for correlation.
observed_logs: 2026-03-11T18:42:09Z Provisioner ERROR: RunInstances failed: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/deployment-runner-role/session is not authorized to perform: iam:PassRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/compute-gpu-role
2026-03-12T03:14:22Z deployment-runner WARN: Retryable error from provisioner: AccessDenied (iam:PassRole) -> retrying (attempt 2)
2026-03-12T03:14:22Z sts DEBUG: AssumeRole succeeded, credentials expire_at=2026-03-12T03:19:22Z
investigation_notes: Confirmed IAM policy attached to deployment-runner-role includes iam:PassRole for target role arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/compute-gpu-role in most cases.
Cross-account role (compute-gpu-role in account 987654321098) has a trusted-entities policy that allows sts:AssumeRole from deployment-runner-role ARN; trust policy looked correct on review.
Failure appears correlated with timing: observed when Provisioner Lambda invoked the RunInstances immediately after AssumeRole, in short bursts of many concurrent attempts.
No recent org-level SCP changes in staging org since 2026-02-26 per org-policy audit logs.

Checked AWS CloudTrail for 'iam:PassRole' denies—found both Allow and Deny events near the timestamps; deny events include condition evaluation details referencing kms:CallerAccount when role had recent session tag injection.
hypothesis: Race between role session tag propagation and policy evaluation across accounts/regions causes transient denies. The deployment-runner flow attaches session tags and immediately calls RunInstances; policy evaluation in target account sometimes sees incomplete tag/session metadata and denies iam:PassRole during the brief window.
workaround: Introduce a 2s linear backoff before the first RunInstances call after AssumeRole (patch applied to staging deployment-runner).
Serialize provisioning bursts by limiting concurrent provisioner invocations to 6 per second for staging GPU pipelines (temporary throttling rule).
resolution: Open - mitigation deployed to staging (2s backoff + concurrency throttle) reduced failure rate from ~12% to <1% in observed window. Root cause still under investigation; next step is to reproduce deterministically and evaluate whether STS/session-tag propagation guarantees are documented/required workaround across AWS accounts.
